scope: DIAGNOSIS: the mere PRESENCE of an entity keeps the client at state 9 - the delta content is irrelevant

the_experiment.mode_5_behaviour: returns 1 without writing any field (a no-op delta)

the_comparison_that_matters: snapshot-single22.bin: count = 0, no entity -> state 10 (the in-match state this project has always reached)
snapshot-ent2 / ent4 / mode1 / mode5: count = 1, one entity -> state 9 in every case
so the presence of an entity is what keeps the client on the loading screen
and it does not depend on what that entity's delta contains, because even a no-op delta gives the same result
the_most_likely_cause: the entity id is 4048, which is out of range for a map like mp_cross_fire (typical CoD entity counts are in the hundreds to low thousands)
a client that cannot resolve an entity in its list will not finish loading, which is exactly the observed behaviour
and the id is fully under our control: it is read as 12 bits from bit 1309
the_decisive_next_experiment: rebuild the body with a SMALL entity id (for example 1, 64 or 100) instead of the arbitrary 4048, keeping everything else identical
if the client then reaches state 10 with count = 1, the id range was the blocker and the entity pipeline is complete
if it stays at 9, the client needs something else besides a valid id, and the search narrows again
why_this_is_progress: it moves the failure from 'the world is not drawn' to 'the entity id is probably out of range', which is a one-line change
it also explains why every entity experiment so far ended on the loading screen: the id was never chosen, it fell out of the bit pattern at 1309
